Bundled FFmpeg dependency compliance manifest

Rook bundles the BtbN FFmpeg-Builds static win64 LGPL 8.1 binary:

https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/autobuild-2026-05-12-13-59/ffmpeg-n8.1.1-win64-lgpl-8.1.zip

That binary is built with external libraries enabled by its FFmpeg configure
line. Rook release validation therefore treats the dependency manifest as a
first-class compliance payload, alongside the FFmpeg license, notice, source,
and provenance files.

The machine-readable dependency manifest is:

ffmpeg-dependencies.json

It records every `--enable-*` configure flag from the bundled binary and ties
the dependency source/build provenance to BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds at commit
28ae7513e7b6477da5c9ba7edb07aa940d485fa2.

Build scripts source archive:

https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/archive/28ae7513e7b6477da5c9ba7edb07aa940d485fa2.zip

Build scripts source SHA-256:

010EED2B486D6EC32E899178EEC51235A151C354B8C81C3C48527A5F412B8DD4

The BtbN build scripts define the external dependency source repositories,
build options, and variant gating used to assemble the LGPL build. Release
validation must fail if the bundled binary's enabled configure flags diverge
from `ffmpeg-dependencies.json`.
